title: Categories fibred in groupoids over a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category ([[def-category]]). A category fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C$ is a functor $p\colon\mathcal S\to\mathcal C$ ([[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]]) such that (i) for every morphism $f\colon V\to U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every object $x$ of $\mathcal S$ over $U$ there exist an object $y$ over $V$ and a morphism $\varphi\colon y\to x$ over $f$, and (ii) every morphism of $\mathcal S$ whose image in $\mathcal C$ is an isomorphism is an isomorphism. A 1-morphism of such categories is a functor over $\mathcal C$; a 2-morphism is a natural transformation over $\mathcal C$ ([[def-natural-transformation]]). For an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ the fibre category $\mathcal S_U$ has as objects the objects over $U$ and as morphisms those over $\mathrm{id}_U$; condition (ii) says that every fibre category is a groupoid ([[def-isomorphism-groupoid-and-connected-category]]). A 1-morphism is an equivalence when it is fully faithful and essentially surjective on fibre categories. Categories fibred in groupoids over $\mathcal C$ form a 2-category, with composition of 1-morphisms associative only up to canonical 2-isomorphisms.
strategy: Definition following Stacks, *Categories*, Sections 4.32-4.35 (tags 001G, 0033, 02XN, 02XO, 02XP, 0038) and Vistoli, Chapter 3, especially Sections 3.3 and 3.5. The formulation by the two axioms is equivalent to the pseudo-functor formulation (Vistoli Section 3.1.2 and Stacks 4.35.2); the 2-category conventions are fixed once and for all. No choice of pullbacks is part of the data; such a choice is used only in explanatory remarks. Equivalence of fibred categories is characterized by fully faithfulness and essential surjectivity on fibre categories (Vistoli Theorem 3.36 / Stacks 4.35.9).
